name: Maxime Descartes Mbogning Fonkou
headline: Research & data analyst, PhD
summary: I turn publication, patent and funding records into evidence people can act on. Ten years of research across Cameroon, France and Canada, from clinical microbiology labs to bibliometrics, patent analytics and data tools.
availability: Open to research-evaluation, data-analysis and public-service roles in Canada

metrics.label: patents mapped for a first-author Nature Biotechnology paper
years of research in Cameroon, France and Canada

about: I started at the lab bench: clinical laboratories in Yaoundé, about 20 new bacterial species described during my PhD in Marseille, then microbiome and cancer research at Gustave Roussy. Ten years of biomedical research showed me how science is really made: who funds it, who publishes it and who patents it.

Now I measure that system. At York University I mapped the global patent landscape of phage therapy, published in Nature Biotechnology. At Simon Fraser University's ScholCommLab I built a harmonised dataset of 7.9 million preprint records from 109 servers.

Through CognosX, the science-intelligence company I founded, I help research teams and biotech companies read publication, patent and funding landscapes, and turn them into decisions. I work in French and English.
